name: Binnenstad (Historic Center)
tagline: Canals, gables and the beating heart of Delft
description: The postcard Delft: a compact grid of tree-lined canals, gabled merchant houses and the Markt square framed by the Nieuwe Kerk and the town hall. Cafes, shops, terraces and history sit at every turn, all within an easy walk or short cycle.
bestFor: Nomads who want to live inside the postcard and walk everywhere
pros: Cafes, terraces and culture on your doorstep
cons: The most expensive and competitive housing in town
Can be busy with tourists and market days

name: TU Delft Campus / Wippolder
tagline: The student and tech engine of the city
description: The area around TU Delft's sprawling campus, buzzing with students, researchers and engineers. Wippolder mixes student housing with a young, international energy, close to campus facilities and a quick cycle from the center. Practical rather than pretty, but full of life.
bestFor: Techies, academics and nomads in the TU Delft orbit
pros: Cheaper and more available housing than the center
Easy cycle to campus and center
cons: Less scenic and more functional in feel
Student turnover can make it feel transient

name: Hof van Delft / Voorhof
description: Established residential districts just outside the center, offering everyday Dutch neighborhood life: apartments, greenery, supermarkets and quiet streets. Hof van Delft sits handily northwest of the center, while Voorhof to the southwest is more modern and higher-density, both an easy bike ride from the canals.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space, calm and better value
pros: Short cycle to the historic center
cons: Lacks the charm and buzz of the center

name: Delfgauw & the Rotterdam / Hague Link
tagline: A calm base plugged into the Randstad
description: Delfgauw is a leafy village just east of Delft, offering greener, quieter living for those who want more space. More broadly, Delft's superb rail and tram links make Rotterdam and The Hague feel like extensions of the city, ideal for commuters or big-city days out.
bestFor: Those wanting quiet space with fast access to bigger cities
pros: Excellent links to Rotterdam and The Hague
cons: More reliant on transport for city life
